problem: Given the curve  $r(t)=⟨{t}^{2},\,4{t}^{2},\,8{t}^{2}⟩,$ $t\ge 0,$ for which the arc length $s$ from $r(0)$ to $r(t)$ is given by $s=9{t}^{2},$ find the corresponding unit tangent $T(s),$ parametrized by $s.$

feedback.problem: Given the curve $r(t)=8t\,i+\operatorname{cos}⁡6t\,j+\operatorname{sin}⁡6t\,k,$ $t\ge 0,$ for which the arc length $s$ from $r(0)$ to $r(t)$ is given by $s=10t,$ find the corresponding unit tangent $T(s),$ parametrized by $s.$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, since $s=10t$, we have that $t=\frac{s}{10}.$

Therefore, the vector function $R(s)$ that parametrizes $r(t)$ by its arc length is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}R(s) & =r(\frac{s}{10}) \\  & =8(\frac{s}{10})\,i+\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{6s}{10})j+\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{6s}{10})k \\  & =\frac{4s}{5}\,i+\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{3s}{5})j+\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{3s}{5})k.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, since the curve is parametrized by its arc length $s$, the unit tangent can be found as

$$
T(s)=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}R(s).
$$

So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}T(s) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}R(s) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{4s}{5})i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{3s}{5}))j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{3s}{5}))k \\  & =\frac{4}{5}\,i-\frac{3}{5}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{3s}{5})j+\frac{3}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{3s}{5})k.\end{aligned}
$$
